curriculumModules.title: CKB fundamentals and the Cell Model
curriculumModules.summary: Build the mental model for live Cells, consumed Cells, capacity, data, and immutable state transitions.
outcomes: Explain why a Cell is immutable after creation
Distinguish live and consumed Cells
Describe how a transaction updates state by consuming inputs and creating outputs
checkpoints: Draw one input Cell becoming receiver and change outputs
Explain where transaction fees come from
Identify lock, type, capacity, and data in a Cell
lab: Run `npm run exercises:run`.
Inspect the transfer and Cell-data practice results.
Write a five-sentence Cell Model explanation in your dev log.

curriculumModules.title: Capacity, data, and occupied bytes
curriculumModules.summary: Understand how CKBytes represent both value and storage capacity, and how Cell data affects required capacity.
outcomes: Convert between CKB and shannons
Explain occupied capacity at a practical level
Encode and decode UTF-8 data stored in a Cell
checkpoints: Calculate shannons for several CKB values
Round-trip a Unicode message through hexadecimal
Explain why extra data increases occupied capacity
lab: Run the local Store Data on Cell model.
Change the sample message to include Vietnamese text.
Record the UTF-8 byte length and hexadecimal payload.

curriculumModules.title: Transaction anatomy and conservation
curriculumModules.summary: Read inputs, outputs, dependencies, witnesses, fees, and transaction status as one coherent state transition.
outcomes: Identify every major transaction component
Check capacity conservation and fee calculation
Explain pending, proposed, committed, and rejected states
checkpoints: Annotate a transaction JSON document
Verify total input capacity equals outputs plus fee
Explain why a returned transaction hash is not final confirmation
lab: Use the local transfer model to inspect sender, receiver, change, and fee.
Create one valid and one insufficient-capacity example.
Write the transaction lifecycle in your own words.

curriculumModules.title: Lock Scripts, Type Scripts, and script groups
curriculumModules.summary: Separate ownership rules from state-transition rules and understand how scripts are grouped and executed.
outcomes: Differentiate Lock and Type Scripts
Explain code_hash, hash_type, and args
Describe why matching scripts are evaluated as groups
checkpoints: Classify three example rules as lock or type logic
Trace script code from a Cell dep
Explain what a non-zero script exit code means
lab: Inspect the credential Type Script configuration in this repository.
Compare the issuer Lock Script with the revocation Type Script.
Record one rule enforced by each script.

curriculumModules.title: Addresses, hashes, and identity binding
curriculumModules.summary: Connect human-readable addresses to lock scripts, and distinguish transaction, script, code, and content hashes.
outcomes: Explain that an address encodes a lock script representation
Distinguish transaction hash from script hash
Use hashes without confusing them with encryption
checkpoints: Decode the role of script args in an address
Label four different hash purposes
Explain why a hash does not reveal a private key
lab: Inspect the configured issuer lock hash.
Compare a credential ID hash with a transaction hash.
Document where each hash is used in verification.

curriculumModules.title: RPC, indexer queries, and transaction status
curriculumModules.summary: Use JSON-RPC safely to query chain state, live Cells, transactions, and indexer results.
outcomes: Construct a JSON-RPC 2.0 request
Choose between direct transaction and indexer queries
Avoid exposing a local node RPC to untrusted networks
checkpoints: Query the tip block number
Query a known transaction status
Explain when indexer search is more appropriate than direct lookup
lab: Start OffCKB and confirm the configured endpoint.
Call one read-only RPC method.
Save the request and redacted response in the dev log.

curriculumModules.title: CCC basics and wallet connections
curriculumModules.summary: Learn the beginner-friendly JavaScript/TypeScript path for connecting wallets and reading CKB state.
outcomes: Explain signer, client, and network roles
Connect a DApp without placing private keys in application code
Read addresses and balances through CCC
checkpoints: Explore the CCC App
Run one Playground example
Record which wallet and network were used without exposing secrets
lab: Open the CCC App and identify network, signer, and address.
Run one read-only Playground example.
Create `learning/ccc-playground/explore-ccc-app.md` from the evidence template.

curriculumModules.title: Building and signing transactions with CCC
curriculumModules.summary: Move from read-only calls to transaction construction, completion, signing, sending, and confirmation.
outcomes: Separate transaction construction from signing
Explain automatic input and fee completion
Track a sent transaction until commitment
checkpoints: Build a transfer transaction
Review outputs before signing
Verify commitment independently after sending
lab: Complete the Transfer CKB official tutorial.
Record sender, receiver, amount, fee, and transaction hash with secrets hidden.
Create the tutorial `completion.md` only after real on-chain success.

curriculumModules.title: Molecule serialization and canonical data
curriculumModules.summary: Understand deterministic binary schemas, canonical encoding, and why on-chain readers and writers must agree byte-for-byte.
outcomes: Explain why deterministic serialization matters
Differentiate fixed and dynamic structures conceptually
Validate a payload before script logic consumes it
checkpoints: Inspect the repository 75-byte credential Cell format
Explain canonical versus malformed encoding
Decode one test vector and compare every field
lab: Run the community vector tests.
Decode a canonical credential Cell.
Mutate one byte and observe validation behavior.

curriculumModules.title: CKB-VM, RISC-V, syscalls, and cycles
curriculumModules.summary: Learn how scripts execute in CKB-VM, load transaction data through syscalls, return exit codes, and consume cycles.
outcomes: Describe the CKB-VM execution boundary
Identify common data-loading syscall purposes
Interpret cycles as execution cost rather than a token fee model
checkpoints: Trace code loading from Cell deps
Map script inputs to syscall reads
Record cycles for one contract test
lab: Run the Rust contract tests when the toolchain is available.
Inspect one syscall in the contract source.
Record the success and one intentional failure exit code.

curriculumModules.title: Rust smart-contract development
curriculumModules.summary: Structure a no-std Rust CKB script, validate arguments and Cell state, and keep error codes deterministic.
outcomes: Navigate a basic Rust script project
Design explicit validation branches and error codes
Write unit and integration tests for valid and invalid transitions
checkpoints: Explain the project entry point
Trace ACTIVE to REVOKED validation
Add one negative test without weakening the protocol
lab: Read the digital-credentials contract.
Run `make test` through the package command.
Document one invariant and the test that proves it.

curriculumModules.title: Testing, debugging, and cycle inspection
curriculumModules.summary: Build a repeatable workflow across unit tests, mock transactions, local Devnet integration, debugger traces, and release checks.
outcomes: Choose the right test layer for a defect
Use CKB Debugger or mock transactions to inspect script failures
Keep release claims tied to reproducible evidence
checkpoints: Run the full local CI suite
Capture one expected contract failure
Explain which tests do and do not require a running node
lab: Run `npm run ci:local`.
Run one deliberately invalid proof or Cell vector.
Write a short defect report with reproduction, expected, and actual behavior.

curriculumModules.title: Payment channels: Fiber and Perun
curriculumModules.summary: Understand why repeated payments can move off-chain while CKB remains the verification and settlement layer.
outcomes: Explain the channel lifecycle at a high level
Differentiate off-chain updates from on-chain settlement
Compare Fiber and Perun as separate CKB payment-channel approaches
checkpoints: Describe open, update, and close phases
Identify what must remain enforceable on-chain
Review one open-source showcase or backend repository
lab: Read the Fiber documentation overview.
Inspect one Fiber showcase project.
Inspect the Perun CKB backend or contracts and record one architectural difference.

curriculumModules.title: Capstone design and evidence planning
curriculumModules.summary: Turn the learning path into a small CKB application with explicit scope, threat boundaries, tests, and weekly evidence.
outcomes: Write a one-page application brief
Define on-chain and off-chain responsibilities
Plan tests, screenshots, and weekly dev-log evidence before implementation
checkpoints: State the user problem and smallest useful flow
List protocol invariants and non-goals
Map every claimed feature to a test or screenshot
lab: Complete `learning/CAPSTONE_BRIEF_TEMPLATE.md`.
Review the idea with the programme director or DevRel.
Add the next week plan to the dev log.
